source: Wording for Approval: Quick-Check Question, Coping Cards and Self-Help Guides (11 Nov 2026), approved by the project psychiatrist. Copied word for word; do not reword. TIP leaves out the temperature step (cold water or ice), in line with approved decision 20.

cards.title: Paced breathing
steps: Sit or stand somewhere steady.
Breathe in gently through your nose for 4 seconds.
Breathe out slowly through your mouth for 6 seconds.
Follow the circle for one minute.
Notice if your body feels even a little calmer.

cards.title: Mindfulness
steps: Look around and name 5 things you can see.
Name 4 things you can touch and feel them.
Name 3 things you can hear.
Name 2 things you can smell.
Name 1 thing you can taste, or take a sip of water.

cards.title: STOP Skill
steps: **Stop.** Pause. Don't act yet.
**Take a step back.** Take one slow breath.
**Observe.** What are you feeling, and what is happening around you?
**Proceed mindfully.** Choose one small step that keeps you safe.

cards.title: TIP Skill (adapted)
steps: **Move.** If it is safe, march on the spot or walk briskly for 1–2 minutes.
**Breathe.** Breathe in for 4, out for 6, five times.
**Tense and release.** Squeeze your hands into fists as you breathe in, then let go as you breathe out. Do the same with your shoulders, then your legs. Notice how your body feels now.

cards.title: Urge surfing
steps: Notice the urge. You don't have to act on it.
Urges are like waves: they rise, peak and pass.
Breathe slowly and watch the urge, without fighting it.
Rate it from 0 to 10, then again in two minutes.
Each time you ride a wave, the next one can feel easier.

cards.title: Reach out
steps: You don't have to go through this alone.
Choose someone from your list, or add one now.
Call or message them: "I'm having a hard time. Can you talk?"
If no one answers, call 800-SAKINA (800 725462), any time.
cards.message: I'm having a hard time. Can you talk?

myReasons.title: My reasons and next steps
steps: Read your reasons for staying safe, or add one now.
Who or what matters to you today?
Choose one next step for the next hour.
If things feel worse, tap "Talk to someone now" or call 998.
